discovery.countNote: Count the folders rather than trusting this number.
discovery.rule: A code has a payload if and only if `support/example_content/<CODE>/manifest.json` exists.
discovery.why: Adding a course code is pure CONTENT — drop in a payload, no code changes anywhere. The existence of the manifest is the whole registration, and it automatically retires that code's generated skeleton.

layout.per_section/: Copied into EVERY sectionN/ the teacher asked for.
layout.shared/: Copied to the course root — folders and files every section shares.

manifestKeys.why: Kept out of the built site — Curriculum and the utility files, in every payload that has them.
Folders the site's explorer opens rather than navigates into.
Names the folder holding expectation pages, so the installer can date and link them. Absent for a course with no curriculum pages.

How many weekdays apart the generated classes sit: 1 for a course that meets daily, 2 for one meeting every other day. The default is 2, so a daily course MUST say so or its classes land on the wrong dates.

note: The ready-made course a teacher can pre-populate: `support/example_content/<CODE>/`. Both apps OFFER these — the wizard asks no structure questions when a payload exists, because the manifest IS the course's entire structure — and the shared Python installs them. So the shape is a contract even though neither app writes it: an app that mis-reads a manifest offers a teacher a course that installs wrong.

rules.rule: The manifest is the WHOLE structure
rules.why: When a payload exists the wizard asks no structure questions at all, so anything missing from the manifest is missing from the course a teacher gets.

rules.detail: `shared/` and `per_section/` may supply content for SOME of what the manifest names; anything named but not shipped is created by the ordinary course scaffolding — a 'Private Notes.md' arrives empty, which is what it should be.
rules.rule: The manifest's lists are an ALLOW-LIST over the payload trees, not a packing list
rules.why: Checked against `setup_course.py` (`top_level_allowed`) after a first draft of this contract asserted the opposite and failed against nine payloads. The lists say what the course HAS; the trees say what arrives with words already in it.

rules.detail: This is the direction that fails silently. ONE exception: `index.md` is always installed without being named, because it is the landing page of the folder it sits in — a section's own front page — and every payload ships one.
rules.rule: Anything IN the payload trees must be named in the manifest
rules.why: `top_level_allowed` filters the copy by those lists, so a folder or file sitting in `shared/` or `per_section/` that the manifest does not name is never installed. The work is in the repository, looks finished, and reaches no teacher.
Mirror its hidden/expandable choices: Curriculum and the utility files hidden, content folders expandable, All Classes visible but not expandable.

rules.detail: `top_level_allowed` requires BOTH that the folder is named in `shared_folders` AND that the teacher chose to include curriculum coverage.
rules.rule: The curriculum folder installs only when the teacher asked for curriculum
rules.why: A teacher who turned coverage off should not be given a folder of expectations they will have to delete.

sentinels.note: A payload ships pages with no dates in them. The installer substitutes these at install time, so a course created in March is not full of a September the teacher never taught.
sentinels.rule: A payload page must carry a sentinel rather than a literal date.

tokens.becomes: the moment the course was created
that class's own meeting date, spread across the section's timetable — which is why `class_weekday_step` exists in the manifest
tokens.meansFor: class pages, where K is the class's index

sentinels.why: A literal date is not merely wrong, it is invisible: the course installs, the pages open, and every class claims a date from whenever the payload was authored. A mac test (`testTheBundledPayloadUsesTheCreatedSentinel`) pins the bundled payload against this.
